passage: Last year, Brightwell Foods replaced the paper menus in 40 of its restaurants with tablet ordering at each table. Average spending per table at those restaurants rose 12 percent over the following six months. On the back of that result, the company's CFO concluded that the tablets, which display photos of high-margin desserts after every main-course order, caused the increase, and she recommends installing them in the chain's remaining 60 locations.
stem: The CFO's argument depends on which of the following assumptions?
choices: Customers at the remaining 60 locations order desserts more often than customers at the original 40 did.
No other change during the six-month period, such as a menu price increase, accounts for most of the rise in per-table spending.
Tablets cost less to maintain than paper menus do.
Most customers prefer ordering on a tablet to ordering from a server.
Spending on desserts rose by a larger percentage than spending on any other menu category.
explanation: The CFO moves from 'spending rose after tablets arrived' to 'tablets caused the rise.' That causal leap only works if nothing else explains the jump. Negate (B): if a price increase drove most of the gain, the tablets did little and the recommendation collapses. That is the signature of a necessary assumption.
keyKR: 전후 비교로 인과를 주장하면, '다른 원인은 없었다'는 전제가 필수예요. 정답 후보를 부정했을 때 결론이 무너지면 그게 가정(assumption)이에요.
trap: (E) sounds supportive because the tablets push desserts, but the argument never needs desserts to be the biggest gainer. A helpful fact is not the same as a required one.

logic.name: Rule out alternative causes
logic.desc: 'A 이후에 B가 일어났다'는 'A가 B를 일으켰다'가 아니에요. 같은 시기의 가격 인상, 계절 효과, 경기 변화 같은 다른 설명을 먼저 지워야 인과가 성립해요.

expr.note: '등 뒤에서'로 직역하면 틀려요. 어떤 결과나 사건이 다음 움직임의 발판이 됐다는 뜻으로 시장 기사와 실적 발표에서 매우 자주 쓰여요.
expr.example: Shares jumped 8% on the back of stronger-than-expected subscriber growth.

passage: As a pilot, a city transit authority cut bus fares by 30 percent on three routes. Within two months, ridership on those routes rose 25 percent. Officials argue that a citywide fare cut would therefore raise total ridership across the bus system by a comparable margin.
stem: Which of the following, if true, most seriously weakens the officials' argument?
choices: Drivers on the pilot routes reported more crowded buses at peak hours during the pilot.
Most of the new riders on the pilot routes had previously ridden nearby parallel routes where the old fares still applied.
The transit authority's budget can absorb the lost fare revenue for at least two years.
Ridership on the pilot routes had been declining slightly in the year before the pilot began.
A survey found that some riders on the pilot routes would have ridden even without the fare cut.
explanation: The officials treat the 25 percent gain as new riding. If most of it came from people abandoning parallel routes, the system as a whole gained little: riders were moved, not created. A citywide cut leaves no cheaper route to switch to, so the pilot overstates the total effect.
keyKR: 일부 노선의 증가가 다른 노선에서 '옮겨온' 것이라면, 전체 시스템의 증가는 거의 없어요. 부분의 성장이 전체의 성장이라는 보장은 없어요.
trap: (D) feels like it matters, but a prior decline actually makes the 25 percent jump look more impressive, so it slightly strengthens the argument.

logic.name: Shift vs. growth
logic.desc: 한 곳의 증가가 다른 곳의 감소로 메워졌다면 전체 효과는 0에 가까워요. 매출, 트래픽, 점유율 수치를 볼 때 늘 '어디서 왔나'를 물어보세요.

expr.note: 원래 뜻(동족을 잡아먹다) 때문에 낯설게 들리지만, 경영 기사에서는 신제품이 기존 제품의 판매를 갉아먹는 상황을 가리키는 표준 용어예요. 이 문제의 파일럿 노선이 바로 인근 노선을 cannibalize한 셈이에요.
expr.example: The cheaper plan grew sign-ups but cannibalized our premium tier, so revenue barely moved.

passage: A survey found that employees at firms offering a four-day workweek reported higher job satisfaction than employees at firms with a standard five-day week. The researchers say the finding bears out the case that adopting a four-day week raises job satisfaction.
stem: Which of the following, if true, most strengthens the researchers' conclusion?
choices: Firms offering a four-day week tend to pay salaries well above the market average.
Employees at four-day firms typically work longer hours on each working day.
At firms that switched to a four-day week, satisfaction scores rose significantly after the switch, while scores at comparable firms that did not switch stayed flat.
Job satisfaction surveys are widely used by human resources departments.
Several firms that tried a four-day week later returned to a five-day schedule.
explanation: The survey is a snapshot comparing different firms, so the satisfaction gap could come from what kind of firm offers a four-day week in the first place. (C) tracks the same firms before and after the change and adds a control group, which isolates the schedule itself as the cause.
keyKR: 서로 다른 회사를 비교한 상관관계만으로는 인과를 말하기 어려워요. 같은 회사의 전후 변화 + 비교군이 있으면 인과 주장이 크게 강해져요.
trap: (A) is a weakener in disguise: higher pay offers a rival explanation for the satisfaction gap.

logic.name: Correlation vs. causation
logic.desc: 좋은 결과를 내는 집단이 애초에 다른 집단일 수 있어요(선택 효과). 전후 비교와 대조군은 인과를 확인하는 가장 강력한 두 도구예요.

expr.note: 'bear(견디다)'와 연결하면 감이 안 와요. 데이터나 사건이 어떤 주장이 맞았음을 보여줄 때 쓰고, 부정형 'not borne out by the data'(데이터로 입증되지 않다)도 자주 나와요.
expr.example: Early sales data have not borne out the team's optimistic forecast.

passage: At Kestrel Analytics, every project whose deadline slipped last quarter was staffed by contractors. Some projects staffed by contractors were nonetheless completed ahead of schedule. No project led by a senior manager missed its deadline last quarter.
stem: If the statements above are true, which of the following must also be true about last quarter?
choices: Some projects completed ahead of schedule were led by senior managers.
Every project that was not staffed by contractors met its deadline.
No project led by a senior manager was staffed by contractors.
Staffing projects with contractors caused deadlines to slip.
Most projects staffed by contractors missed their deadlines.
explanation: The first sentence says: missed deadline → contractors. Its contrapositive is: no contractors → did not miss. That is exactly (B). The other choices either reverse the conditional, assume a causal link, or claim proportions the passage never gives.
keyKR: 'A면 B다'가 참이면 'B가 아니면 A도 아니다'(대우)도 반드시 참이에요. 하지만 'B면 A다'(역)는 보장되지 않아요.
trap: (C) feels natural because senior-led projects never slipped, but a senior-led project could have used contractors and still finished on time.

logic.name: Contrapositive
logic.desc: '마감을 놓친 프로젝트는 모두 외주였다' → '외주가 아니면 마감을 지켰다'. 역(외주면 마감을 놓쳤다)으로 착각하는 게 가장 흔한 실수예요.

expr.note: '미끄러지다'의 직역 대신 일정·출시일이 조금씩 뒤로 밀리는 상황에 원어민이 아주 흔히 써요. 사람 주어로 'let it slip'(놓치다)과는 뉘앙스가 달라요.
expr.example: The launch date has already slipped twice, so let's not commit to Q1 publicly.

passage: A national grocery chain plans to replace most of its cashiers with self-checkout kiosks. Management argues that the labor savings will raise the chain's profits.
stem: Which of the following would be most useful to know in evaluating management's argument?
choices: Whether the chain's cashiers are, on average, older than those at competing chains
Whether competing chains have already installed self-checkout kiosks
Whether higher shrinkage at self-checkout, from theft and scanning errors, would offset the labor savings
How many kiosks can fit in the floor space currently used by staffed checkout lanes
Whether customers in the chain's urban stores shop more often than those in suburban stores
explanation: The argument looks only at one side of the ledger: lower labor cost. Profit depends on the net effect. If losses from theft and errors grow by more than the savings, profits fall. The answer to (C) could flip the conclusion either way, which is what an evaluate question asks for.
keyKR: 비용 절감 → 이익 증가 논리에는 '새로 생기는 비용'이 빠지기 쉬워요. 답이 '예/아니오'에 따라 결론이 뒤집히는 질문이 정답이에요.
trap: (B) is interesting context, but whatever competitors did, it does not tell you whether this chain's profits will rise.

logic.name: Net, not gross
logic.desc: 절감액(gross)만 보면 항상 좋아 보여요. 새 방식이 만드는 추가 비용을 빼야 실제 효과(net)가 나와요. Evaluate 문제는 이 숨은 변수를 찾는 게임이에요.

expr.note: 일반 영어에서는 '줄어듦'이지만, 소매업에서는 도난·파손·계산 오류로 장부보다 재고가 비는 손실을 뜻하는 업계 용어예요. 유통사 실적 발표에서 자주 나와요.
expr.example: Retailers blamed higher shrinkage for squeezing margins in the third quarter.

passage: Critics of the new data-privacy law argue that it will hurt the technology industry. But the law's compliance costs come to roughly $50,000 per company per year, a rounding error for the large firms that dominate the market. Therefore, the law will not place a meaningful burden on companies in the industry.
stem: The reasoning in the argument is most vulnerable to criticism on the grounds that it
choices: relies on a cost estimate supplied by the law's critics
draws a conclusion about all companies in the industry from evidence about only the largest firms
assumes that the law will be strictly enforced
fails to consider that large firms may pass compliance costs on to customers
treats a decrease in costs as though it were an increase in profits
explanation: The evidence covers only the giants, for whom $50,000 is trivial. The conclusion covers 'companies in the industry,' which includes startups for whom the same fixed fee may be a large share of their budget. The argument quietly widens its scope from a subset to the whole.
keyKR: 근거는 '대기업'에 대한 것인데 결론은 '업계 전체'에 대해 말해요. 근거와 결론의 범위가 다르면 그게 결함이에요.
trap: (D) describes a real-world possibility, but even if true it would not expose a gap in this argument's logic.

logic.name: Scope shift
logic.desc: 고정비는 규모가 작을수록 부담이 커요. 일부 집단에 대한 근거로 전체를 결론 내리면, 빠진 집단에서 결론이 깨질 수 있어요.

expr.note: 수학 용어지만 비즈니스에서는 '전체 규모에 비해 무시해도 될 정도로 작은 돈'을 가리키는 관용 표현이에요. 비꼬는 뉘앙스로도 써요.
expr.example: For a company with $90 billion in revenue, that fine is a rounding error.

passage:
For decades, economists treated the loss leader, a product sold below cost to draw customers in, as a retail curiosity: the supermarket that discounts milk so shoppers will fill their carts with higher-margin goods. Digital platforms turned the tactic into a strategy. Ride-hailing and food-delivery companies subsidized prices for years, betting that once users formed habits and drivers clustered on the platform, network effects would let prices rise without driving customers away.

The record so far is mixed. Some platforms did reach enough scale to raise prices, and their margins improved. Others found that the habits they had paid for were shallower than expected: when subsidies ended, a meaningful share of users simply moved to whichever rival was still discounting. The difference, several analysts argue, lies less in scale than in switching costs. A platform whose users have stored years of data, reviews, or social connections on it can afford to stop subsidizing; one whose service is easily replicated cannot, however large it has grown.

The distinction matters for regulators as well. If dominance rests on switching costs rather than on size alone, then rules that make user data portable may do more to restrain pricing power than attempts to break up large firms.
stem: The primary purpose of the passage is to
choices: argue that loss-leader pricing is unprofitable for digital platforms
explain why subsidy-driven growth paid off for some platforms but not others, and draw an implication for regulation
compare supermarket pricing practices with those of digital platforms in detail
criticize regulators for overlooking the role of network effects
recommend that platforms stop subsidizing prices
explanation: Paragraph 1 sets up the strategy, paragraph 2 explains the split in outcomes (switching costs, not scale), and paragraph 3 applies that to regulation. (B) captures all three moves. (A) is too extreme: the author says some platforms succeeded.
keyKR: 주제 문제는 각 문단이 하는 '역할'을 한 줄씩 정리한 뒤, 그걸 모두 덮는 보기를 고르면 돼요. 너무 좁거나 너무 강한 보기는 탈락이에요.
trap: (C) is tempting because the supermarket appears first, but it is only a brief opening example, not the focus.

logic.name: Map the paragraphs
logic.desc: 긴 지문은 '설정 → 반전/구분 → 함의'처럼 문단 기능으로 요약해요. 주장의 뼈대를 먼저 잡으면 세부 문제도 빨라져요.

expr.kr: 미끼 상품(손해 보고 파는 집객용 상품)
expr.note: '손실 리더'로 직역하면 이상해요. 원가 이하로 팔아 고객을 끌어들이고 다른 상품에서 이익을 내는 전략 상품을 뜻하는 표준 비즈니스 용어예요.
expr.example: The console is basically a loss leader; the real money is in games and subscriptions.

passage:
For decades, economists treated the loss leader, a product sold below cost to draw customers in, as a retail curiosity: the supermarket that discounts milk so shoppers will fill their carts with higher-margin goods. Digital platforms turned the tactic into a strategy. Ride-hailing and food-delivery companies subsidized prices for years, betting that once users formed habits and drivers clustered on the platform, network effects would let prices rise without driving customers away.

The record so far is mixed. Some platforms did reach enough scale to raise prices, and their margins improved. Others found that the habits they had paid for were shallower than expected: when subsidies ended, a meaningful share of users simply moved to whichever rival was still discounting. The difference, several analysts argue, lies less in scale than in switching costs. A platform whose users have stored years of data, reviews, or social connections on it can afford to stop subsidizing; one whose service is easily replicated cannot, however large it has grown.

The distinction matters for regulators as well. If dominance rests on switching costs rather than on size alone, then rules that make user data portable may do more to restrain pricing power than attempts to break up large firms.
stem: It can be inferred from the passage that the author would most likely agree with which of the following?
choices: A very large platform whose service is easy to copy may still struggle to raise prices after ending subsidies.
Breaking up large technology firms would have no effect on their pricing power.
Supermarkets have largely stopped using loss leaders.
Network effects play no role in a platform's ability to raise prices.
Rules that make user data portable would raise platforms' profit margins.
explanation: The author says a platform with an easily replicated service cannot stop subsidizing, however large it has grown. (A) restates that directly. (B) overreaches: the author only says portability 'may do more' than breakups, not that breakups do nothing.
keyKR: 추론 문제의 정답은 지문에서 한 걸음만 나아간 보기예요. 'no effect', 'no role' 같은 극단적 표현은 대부분 함정이에요.
trap: (B) twists a comparison ('may do more than') into an absolute ('no effect').

logic.name: Comparative ≠ absolute
logic.desc: 'X가 Y보다 효과적일 수 있다'는 'Y는 효과가 없다'가 아니에요. 비교를 절대 주장으로 바꾼 보기는 거의 항상 오답이에요.

expr.kr: 전환 비용(다른 서비스로 옮길 때 드는 비용·불편)
expr.note: 돈뿐 아니라 데이터, 습관, 인맥처럼 옮기기 번거로운 모든 것을 포함해요. 테크 기업 분석에서 'moat(해자)'를 설명할 때 핵심으로 등장하는 개념이에요.
expr.example: Our enterprise clients stay because the switching costs of migrating years of data are enormous.

passage:
Through the 1990s and 2000s, manufacturers embraced just-in-time inventory, holding only the parts needed for immediate production. The approach freed up cash and exposed inefficiencies that large stockpiles had masked. Yet it also stripped away the buffers that once absorbed shocks, and when pandemic-era disruptions hit, firms with the leanest inventories were often the first to halt production.

Many commentators predicted that companies would swing back to a "just-in-case" model and stockpile critical inputs across the board. The evidence points to a more selective adjustment. Surveys of procurement managers show that firms have raised safety stocks mainly for components that have few suppliers or long lead times, while keeping inventories lean for parts that can be sourced quickly from multiple vendors.

The lesson most firms drew, then, was that the costs of efficiency had been mispriced rather than that efficiency itself was a mistake. The savings from holding less inventory showed up on every balance sheet, while the risk of a production stoppage stayed invisible until it materialized.
stem: The author mentions surveys of procurement managers primarily in order to
choices: prove that just-in-time inventory is now obsolete
support the claim that firms adjusted their inventory policies selectively rather than across the board
show that commentators correctly predicted a broad return to stockpiling
estimate how much pandemic disruptions cost manufacturers
argue that firms with many suppliers suffered the worst shortages
explanation: Right before the surveys, the author says the evidence points to a 'more selective adjustment.' The surveys supply that evidence: safety stock went up for scarce, slow parts but stayed lean for easily sourced ones. (C) is the opposite: the surveys undercut the commentators.
keyKR: '왜 이 내용을 언급했나' 문제는 그 문장 바로 앞뒤의 주장을 찾으면 돼요. 근거는 늘 어떤 주장을 받치기 위해 존재해요.
trap: (C) reuses words from the passage (commentators, stockpiling) but reverses the author's point.

logic.name: Evidence serves a claim
logic.desc: 데이터·사례·인용이 나오면 '이게 어떤 주장을 받치나?'를 먼저 물어보세요. 보고서를 읽을 때도 그대로 쓰이는 습관이에요.

expr.note: 그네처럼 반대 방향으로 크게 넘어갔다 돌아오는 느낌이 있어요. 정책, 시장 심리, 경영 트렌드가 반대로 크게 움직일 때 원어민이 자주 써요.
expr.example: After two years of remote-first hiring, many firms have swung back to requiring office attendance.

passage:
Through the 1990s and 2000s, manufacturers embraced just-in-time inventory, holding only the parts needed for immediate production. The approach freed up cash and exposed inefficiencies that large stockpiles had masked. Yet it also stripped away the buffers that once absorbed shocks, and when pandemic-era disruptions hit, firms with the leanest inventories were often the first to halt production.

Many commentators predicted that companies would swing back to a "just-in-case" model and stockpile critical inputs across the board. The evidence points to a more selective adjustment. Surveys of procurement managers show that firms have raised safety stocks mainly for components that have few suppliers or long lead times, while keeping inventories lean for parts that can be sourced quickly from multiple vendors.

The lesson most firms drew, then, was that the costs of efficiency had been mispriced rather than that efficiency itself was a mistake. The savings from holding less inventory showed up on every balance sheet, while the risk of a production stoppage stayed invisible until it materialized.
stem: Based on the passage, a manufacturer would be most likely to raise its safety stock of which of the following?
choices: A standard fastener available from dozens of domestic vendors
A specialized chip made by a single overseas supplier with a six-month lead time
Office supplies used by the administrative staff
A part the company already holds in surplus
A component whose market price recently fell
explanation: The passage says safety stocks rose mainly for components with few suppliers or long lead times. A single-source chip with a six-month lead time meets both conditions. The fastener in (A) is the passage's example of what stays lean.
keyKR: 적용 문제는 지문의 '기준'을 뽑아 새 상황에 대입해요. 여기선 '공급처가 적다 + 리드타임이 길다'가 기준이에요.
trap: (E) sounds like a good buying opportunity, but the passage's logic is about supply risk, not price.

logic.name: Extract the rule, then apply
logic.desc: 사례에서 일반 규칙을 뽑고, 새 사례가 그 조건을 충족하는지 확인해요. 정책·가이드라인을 실무에 적용할 때와 같은 사고예요.

expr.note: 실제 가격표가 틀렸다는 뜻보다, 시장이나 조직이 어떤 위험이나 가치를 과소·과대평가했다는 의미로 금융·전략 글에서 많이 써요.
expr.example: Investors argue that credit risk in that sector has been badly mispriced for years.

passage: A software company sold annual licenses at exactly two prices last year: $400 for a standard license and $250 for a discounted license.
stem:
What was the company's total revenue from licenses last year?
(1) The company sold 1,200 licenses in total.
(2) Discounted licenses made up 30 percent of all licenses sold.
choices: Statement (1) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (2) alone is not sufficient.
Statement (2) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (1) alone is not sufficient.
BOTH statements TOGETHER are sufficient, but NEITHER statement ALONE is sufficient.
EACH statement ALONE is sufficient.
Statements (1) and (2) TOGETHER are NOT sufficient.
explanation: (1) gives the count but not the mix, so revenue could range from $300,000 to $480,000. (2) gives the mix but not the count. Together: 840 standard and 360 discounted, so revenue = 840 × $400 + 360 × $250 = $426,000. You do not even need to finish the arithmetic, only to know a single value exists.
keyKR: DS는 답을 '계산'하는 게 아니라 '유일한 값이 정해지는가'만 판단해요. 값이 하나로 정해지는 순간 멈추세요.
trap: Some people pick (A) because 1,200 feels like 'the data.' Without the mix, the total can vary widely.

logic.name: Sufficiency, not solving
logic.desc: 결론을 내리기에 정보가 충분한지 판단하는 능력이에요. 회의에서 '이 데이터로 결론 내려도 되나?'를 묻는 것과 같은 사고예요.

expr.note: 여러 가격·금리가 섞였을 때의 평균값을 말해요. 이 문제에서는 라이선스당 평균 $355가 blended rate예요. 컨설팅 비용, 대출 금리 논의에서 자주 나와요.
expr.example: With the junior staff on the team, our blended rate comes down to about $210 an hour.

passage: Company X was profitable in both 2025 and 2026. Operating margin is defined as operating income divided by revenue.
stem:
Did Company X's operating margin increase from 2025 to 2026?
(1) Operating income growth outpaced revenue growth from 2025 to 2026.
(2) Revenue grew 15 percent from 2025 to 2026.
choices: Statement (1) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (2) alone is not sufficient.
Statement (2) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (1) alone is not sufficient.
BOTH statements TOGETHER are sufficient, but NEITHER statement ALONE is sufficient.
EACH statement ALONE is sufficient.
Statements (1) and (2) TOGETHER are NOT sufficient.
explanation: The new margin equals the old margin × (1 + income growth) / (1 + revenue growth). If income grew faster than revenue, that ratio is above 1, so the margin rose. (1) alone answers 'yes' without any actual numbers. (2) alone says nothing about income.
keyKR: 비율이 오르는지는 분자와 분모의 '성장률 비교'만으로 판단돼요. 구체적인 숫자가 없어도 충분할 수 있어요.
trap: Many people choose (C) because they feel they need a concrete revenue number. A 'yes/no' question only needs a definite direction.

logic.name: Ratios move with relative growth
logic.desc: 이익률, 점유율, 1인당 지표는 분자가 분모보다 빨리 크면 올라가요. 실적 기사를 읽을 때 수치 없이도 방향을 판단하는 도구예요.

expr.note: 경쟁자를 이긴다는 뜻보다, 두 지표의 증가 속도를 비교할 때 경제 기사에서 정말 자주 써요. 'wage growth outpaced inflation' 같은 형태가 대표적이에요.
expr.example: Wage growth has outpaced inflation for six straight months.

passage: The table shows revenue for a company's four regional divisions in 2025 and 2026, along with each division's headcount at the end of 2026. Tap a column heading to sort.
stem: For each of the following statements, select Yes if the statement is true based on the information provided. Otherwise, select No.
explanation: Statement 1: growth is North 15%, South 10%, East 4%, West 25%, so Yes. Statement 2: East has the most revenue ($156M) but the lowest revenue per employee (about $260K), so No. Statement 3: North (about $345K) and West (about $326K) both clear $320K, so Yes. On the real exam you must get all three right to earn credit.
keyKR: Table Analysis는 세 문장을 모두 맞혀야 점수를 받아요. 정렬 기능으로 필요한 열만 빠르게 비교하고, 비율은 어림셈으로 판단하세요.
trap: Statement 2 tempts you to assume the biggest division is also the most efficient. Size and efficiency are separate measures.

logic.name: Check each condition separately
logic.desc: '가장 큰 곳이 가장 효율적이다' 같은 연결은 데이터로 따로 확인해야 해요. 규모와 효율은 별개의 지표예요.

expr.note: 손익계산서 맨 위가 매출이라 top line, 맨 아래가 순이익이라 bottom line이에요. 'top-line growth but weak margins'처럼 둘을 대비해서 자주 써요.
expr.example: The division delivered strong top-line growth, but margins are still under pressure.

statements: The West division had the highest percentage revenue growth from 2025 to 2026.
The division with the highest 2026 revenue also had the highest 2026 revenue per employee.
At least two divisions generated more than $320,000 of 2026 revenue per employee.

passage: A consulting firm bills Associates at $150 per hour and Managers at $250 per hour. For one client engagement, the firm billed exactly 100 hours in total for exactly $18,000.
stem: Select for Associate hours the number of hours billed by Associates, and select for Manager hours the number of hours billed by Managers. Make only two selections, one in each column.
explanation: Let a be Associate hours. Then 150a + 250(100 − a) = 18,000, so 25,000 − 100a = 18,000 and a = 70. Managers billed 30 hours. Check: 70 × 150 + 30 × 250 = 10,500 + 7,500 = 18,000.
keyKR: Two-Part는 두 열이 같은 선택지를 공유해요. 조건마다 식을 하나씩 세우면 두 칸이 동시에 정해져요.
trap: Swapping the columns (30 Associate, 70 Manager) is the classic slip: you solve correctly and then click the wrong column.

logic.name: One constraint, one equation
logic.desc: 미지수가 두 개면 독립된 조건도 두 개 필요해요. 예산 배분이나 인력 계획에서도 '조건이 몇 개인가'부터 세면 문제가 정리돼요.

expr.kr: 청구 가능 시간(고객에게 비용을 청구할 수 있는 근무 시간)
expr.note: 컨설팅·로펌·회계법인의 핵심 지표예요. 내부 회의나 교육 시간은 non-billable로 구분하고, 'utilization(가동률)'과 함께 자주 쓰여요.
expr.example: Our associates are expected to log about 1,800 billable hours a year.

stem: A retailer prices an item at 40 percent above its cost, then offers a 25 percent discount on that price. The final selling price is what percent of the cost?
explanation: Final price = cost × 1.40 × 0.75 = cost × 1.05, so 105 percent of cost. A 40 percent markup followed by a 25 percent discount does not net to +15 percent, because the discount applies to a larger base.
keyKR: 연속된 퍼센트 변화는 더하지 말고 곱해요. 1.4 × 0.75 = 1.05.
trap: (E) comes from simply subtracting 25 from 40.

logic.name: Percent changes multiply
logic.desc: +40% 후 −25%는 +15%가 아니에요. 할인이 더 큰 기준값에 적용되기 때문이에요. 수익률이나 가격 협상에서 자주 하는 착각이에요.

expr.note: 같은 이익이라도 기준이 달라요. 원가 100, 판매가 140이면 markup은 40%, margin은 약 28.6%예요. 실무에서 섞어 쓰다 숫자 오해가 자주 생겨요.
expr.example: A 50% markup sounds generous, but it's only a 33% margin once you do the math.

stem: An app's monthly active users grew from 8,000 to 12,500 over two months, growing by the same percentage each month. What was the monthly growth rate?
explanation: If the monthly growth factor is g, then 8,000 × g² = 12,500, so g² = 1.5625 and g = 1.25. That is 25 percent per month: 8,000 → 10,000 → 12,500.
keyKR: 같은 비율로 n번 성장하면 '곱하기 n번'이에요. 총 증가율(56.25%)을 2로 나누면 안 돼요.
trap: (D) halves the total 56.25 percent increase, which ignores compounding.

logic.name: Compounding
logic.desc: 기간별 성장률은 총 성장률을 나눠서 구하지 않고 제곱근(또는 n제곱근)으로 구해요. 연평균 성장률(CAGR)과 같은 원리예요.

expr.note: 비슷하게 YoY(전년 동기 대비), QoQ(전분기 대비)도 있어요. 성장 지표를 보고할 때 어떤 기준으로 비교한 건지 명시하는 게 원어민 실무 습관이에요.
expr.example: Active users grew 25% month-over-month, but YoY growth is closer to 140%.

passage: Over the past five years, a regional airline's on-time arrival rate has improved from 71 percent to 84 percent. Over the same period, however, the number of customer complaints the airline receives about delays has risen steadily.
stem: Which of the following, if true, most helps to resolve the apparent discrepancy described above?
choices: Customer complaints about lost baggage at the airline also rose during the same period.
The airline lengthened the scheduled duration of many routes, so more flights now arrive 'on time' even though actual travel times have grown.
Competing airlines' on-time arrival rates improved by similar amounts during the period.
The airline's passenger volume doubled over the period, and the percentage of passengers who complained about delays also rose.
Industry analysts regard an on-time arrival rate above 80 percent as excellent.
explanation: The puzzle is that the delay metric improved while delay complaints grew. (B) shows the metric and the passenger experience came apart: padding the schedule lets more flights count as on time even though trips take longer, which is exactly what travelers complain about.
keyKR: 모순 해결 문제의 정답은 두 사실이 '동시에' 참일 수 있게 만드는 보기예요. 지표가 좋아졌는데 불만이 늘었다면, 지표가 실제 경험을 반영하지 못하게 된 이유를 찾으세요.
trap: (D) looks like a volume explanation, but it adds that the share of complaining passengers also rose, so the puzzle remains.

logic.name: Metric vs. reality
logic.desc: 지표가 목표가 되면 사람들은 실제 성과 대신 지표를 관리하기 시작해요(굿하트의 법칙). KPI가 좋아졌는데 현장 반응이 나쁘면 지표 정의부터 의심하세요.

expr.note: '패드를 대다'가 아니라, 일부러 넉넉하게 잡아 두는 걸 말해요. 좋은 의미(버퍼)와 나쁜 의미(부풀리기) 둘 다로 쓰여서 문맥을 봐야 해요.
expr.example: I padded the timeline by a week because legal review always takes longer than promised.

passage: The chart shows a streaming company's quarterly revenue in 2026.
stem: Select the option from each drop-down menu that creates the most accurate statement based on the information provided.
sentence: From Q1 to Q4, revenue grew by approximately {0}, and the largest quarter-over-quarter increase in dollar terms occurred between {1}.
explanation: 66 ÷ 48 = 1.375, so revenue grew about 38 percent. The quarterly increases are $4M, $8M and $6M, so the largest dollar jump was from Q2 to Q3, even though Q4 has the tallest bar.
keyKR: 그래프 문제는 '가장 높은 막대'와 '가장 큰 증가폭'을 구분하는 게 핵심이에요. 증가폭은 막대 사이의 차이로 봐요.
trap: The eye goes to the tallest bar (Q4), but the question asks about the biggest change, not the biggest level.

logic.name: Level vs. change
logic.desc: 가장 큰 값과 가장 많이 변한 구간은 다를 수 있어요. 실적 발표에서 '사상 최대 매출'과 '성장 둔화'가 동시에 나오는 이유예요.

expr.note: 실적 발표에서 sequentially는 '연속해서'가 아니라 '바로 전 분기와 비교해'라는 뜻이에요. 전년 동기 대비(year over year)와 대비해서 많이 써요.
expr.example: Revenue rose 15% sequentially, though year-over-year growth slowed to 9%.

tabs.title: CFO memo
tabs.text:
We currently run our analytics workloads in our own data center at a fixed cost of $2.4 million per year. The cloud provider we are evaluating charges an annual platform fee plus a usage fee.

I will approve the move only if two conditions hold: projected cloud costs for next year must be at least 15 percent below our current cost, and the plan's committed uptime must be at least 99.9 percent.

tabs.title: Pricing
tabs.text: The provider offers three plans. Usage is billed per 1,000 compute-hours.

tabs.title: Usage forecast
tabs.text: The engineering team projects 1,100,000 compute-hours next year. If a planned product launch succeeds, usage could run as much as 20 percent above that forecast.

stem: Based on the forecast usage of 1,100,000 compute-hours, which plan or plans would satisfy both of the CFO's conditions?
choices: Basic only
Standard only
Premium only
Standard and Premium
None of the plans
explanation: The cost ceiling is 85% of $2.4M = $2.04M. At 1,100 thousand hours: Basic = $0.3M + $1.65M = $1.95M, Standard = $0.6M + $1.32M = $1.92M, Premium = $0.9M + $1.10M = $2.00M. All three pass on cost, but Basic fails the 99.9% uptime condition, leaving Standard and Premium.
keyKR: MSR은 탭마다 흩어진 조건을 모아야 풀려요. 메모(조건) → 가격표(계산) → 예측(입력값) 순서로 정리하면 빨라요.
trap: Basic is cheap enough, so it is easy to stop at the cost test and forget the uptime condition in the first tab.

logic.name: Gather every constraint first
logic.desc: 여러 자료에 흩어진 조건을 먼저 목록으로 만들고 계산은 나중에 해요. 의사결정 문서를 읽을 때도 '승인 조건'을 먼저 뽑는 습관이 실수를 줄여줘요.

expr.note: 원래 머리 위 공간이지만, 비즈니스에서는 예산·용량·규제 한도까지 남은 여유를 뜻해요. 이 문제에서 Premium은 비용 상한까지 $40K의 headroom밖에 없어요.
expr.example: We have very little headroom in the budget if the launch slips into Q2.

tabs.title: CFO memo
tabs.text:
We currently run our analytics workloads in our own data center at a fixed cost of $2.4 million per year. The cloud provider we are evaluating charges an annual platform fee plus a usage fee.

I will approve the move only if two conditions hold: projected cloud costs for next year must be at least 15 percent below our current cost, and the plan's committed uptime must be at least 99.9 percent.

tabs.title: Pricing
tabs.text: The provider offers three plans. Usage is billed per 1,000 compute-hours.

tabs.title: Usage forecast
tabs.text: The engineering team projects 1,100,000 compute-hours next year. If a planned product launch succeeds, usage could run as much as 20 percent above that forecast.

stem: For each of the following statements, select Yes if the statement can be shown to be true based on the information provided. Otherwise, select No.
statements: If usage runs 20 percent above the forecast, none of the three plans would meet the CFO's cost condition.
At forecast usage, the Premium plan would cost less than the Standard plan.
At forecast usage, the Basic plan would be the least expensive of the three plans.
explanation: At 1,320 thousand hours (20% above forecast): Basic $2.28M, Standard $2.184M, Premium $2.22M, all above the $2.04M ceiling, so Yes. At forecast usage, Standard ($1.92M) is cheaper than Premium ($2.00M) and also cheaper than Basic ($1.95M), so statements 2 and 3 are both No.
keyKR: 낮은 고정비 플랜이 항상 싸다고 가정하지 마세요. 사용량이 많으면 단위 요금이 낮은 플랜이 역전해요. 시나리오가 바뀌면 숫자를 다시 계산해야 해요.
trap: Basic has the lowest platform fee, so it feels cheapest. At this volume the higher usage fee outweighs that advantage.

logic.name: Fixed vs. variable cost
logic.desc: 고정비가 낮고 변동비가 높은 옵션은 사용량이 적을 때만 유리해요. 손익분기점이 어디인지 알면 시나리오별 판단이 쉬워져요.

expr.note: 은행 건전성 평가에서 나온 말이지만, 일상 업무에서도 '조건이 나빠져도 버티는지 따져보자'는 뜻으로 아주 자주 써요.
expr.example: Before we sign, let's stress-test the budget against a 20% jump in usage.
